So digits are 0-6 valid, 7 is INVALID_DIGIT. The digit tables are `[7][7]`, indexed by `oldDigit` (0-6) and `dir` (0-6). If `oldDigit` is 7 (INVALID_DIGIT), then `NEW_DIGIT_II[7][dir]` would be out of bounds (index 7 in a 7-element array).

The `H3_GET_INDEX_DIGIT` returns a value 0-7 (3 bits). So if the index has a digit value of 7 in some resolution position, then in `h3NeighborRotations`, `oldDigit = H3_GET_INDEX_DIGIT(out, r+1)` could be 7, and `NEW_DIGIT_II[oldDigit][dir]` would read out of bounds.

Let me look at `_h3LeadingNonZeroDigit` and how the fuzzer input is structured. The fuzzer reads `{H3Index index; int k;}`. The index is a 64-bit value. We need to craft an index with an invalid digit (7) in a position that gets processed.

Let me look at `_h3LeadingNonZeroDigit` and `isResolutionClassIII`.
